extracted.intended_audience: USPTO-registered patent practitioners, attorneys/agents before the USPTO, and legal professionals interested in USPTO disciplinary procedures
extracted.subtask_description: Standards and procedural requirements governing reciprocal discipline of persons admitted to practice before the USPTO (imposition of discipline based on state disciplinary actions, required notices, and operational effects of suspension).

rubrics_metrics.name: Reciprocal discipline under 37 C.F.R. § 11.24
rubrics_metrics.description: The Director filed a 'Complaint for Reciprocal Discipline Pursuant to 37 C.F.R. § 11.24' requesting that the Director of the USPTO impose reciprocal discipline upon Respondent identical to the discipline imposed by the State court.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: USPTO may impose discipline identical to that imposed by a state court pursuant to 37 C.F.R. § 11.24; the Complaint initiating reciprocal discipline will be served via a Notice and Order and triggers procedural rights described in that regulation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Opportunity to respond (40 days) under the Notice and Order
rubrics_metrics.description: The Notice and Order provided Respondent an opportunity to file, within forty (40) days, a response opposing the imposition of reciprocal discipline identical to that imposed by the State, based on one or more of the reasons provided in 37 C.F.R. § 11.24(d)(1).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Service of the Notice and Order starts the 40-day response period; the response must assert one or more of the specific grounds in 11.24(d)(1) to oppose identical discipline. Timely filing is required to raise contested factual or legal issues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of failure to respond under 37 C.F.R. § 11.24(d)
rubrics_metrics.description: In light of Respondent's failure to file a response, it is determined that there is no genuine issue of material fact under 37 C.F.R. § 11.24(d) and Respondent's suspension from practice before the USPTO is the appropriate discipline.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Failure to timely respond can result in a determination that no genuine issue of material fact exists and lead to imposition of reciprocal discipline without further contested proceedings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Violation predicate: 37 C.F.R. § 11.804(h)
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent's reciprocal discipline is predicated on his violation of 37 C.F.R. § 11.804(h), having been disciplined by a duly constituted authority of a state.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Being disciplined by a state authority can constitute a violation of the USPTO disciplinary rules (specifically § 11.804(h)), which may support reciprocal action by the Office.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statutory/regulatory authority for USPTO action
rubrics_metrics.description: This action is taken pursuant to the provisions of 35 U.S.C. § 32 and 37 C.F.R. § 11.24.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: USPTO disciplinary actions rest on federal statute (35 U.S.C. § 32) and the implementing regulations in 37 C.F.R. part 11; any discipline imposed should cite these authorities as the basis for action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication of Notice in the Official Gazette
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED Director shall publish a Notice in the Official Gazette describing the suspension, the basis for it, respondent's registration number, prior disciplinary history, and reference to availability of decisions at the OED FOIA Reading Room.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Office will publish a public notice summarizing the discipline and reasons (example language provided). Such publication includes identifying information (name, registration number), the rule violated, predicate state discipline, and links/locations for the full disciplinary decision.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice to state disciplinary agencies and courts under 37 C.F.R. § 11.59
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED Director shall give notice pursuant to 37 C.F.R. § 11.59 of the public discipline and the reasons for the discipline to disciplinary enforcement agencies in the state(s) where Respondent is admitted to practice, to courts where Respondent is known to be admitted, and to the public.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: USPTO must notify relevant state disciplinary bodies and courts of imposed discipline and its reasons, ensuring cross-jurisdictional awareness of the sanction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Duties upon suspension under 37 C.F.R. § 11.58
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent shall comply with the duties enumerated in 37 C.F.R. § 11.58.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Although specifics are not enumerated in this Order, § 11.58 outlines obligations of a suspended practitioner (e.g., notification of clients, withdrawal/transfer of matters, notification to the Office); suspended practitioners must follow those enumerated duties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dissociation from USPTO Customer Numbers and PKI certificates
rubrics_metrics.description: The USPTO shall dissociate Respondent's name from any Customer Numbers and the public key infrastructure ("PKI") certificate associated with those Customer Numbers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Operational remedies for suspension include removing the practitioner's association with USPTO electronic account identifiers and revoking any PKI certificates to prevent electronic filing/authentication by the suspended individual.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on obtaining or being added to a Customer Number until reinstatement
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent shall not apply for a USPTO Customer Number, shall not obtain a USPTO Customer Number, nor shall he have his name added to a USPTO Customer Number, unless and until he is reinstated to practice before the USPTO.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Suspension includes a bar on acquiring or re-acquiring access to USPTO customer accounts or being added to such accounts until formal reinstatement; attempts to circumvent this are prohibited.

rubrics_metrics.name: State-court-disciplined conduct examples supporting reciprocal discipline
rubrics_metrics.description: The State court found respondent's misconduct in New Jersey constituted violations of Rule 8.4(d) (misconduct by engaging in conduct prejudicial to the administration of justice); the Court also noted failure to advise the Attorney Grievance Committee of his New Jersey suspension, persistent registration delinquencies spanning four registration periods, and failure to participate in the disciplinary proceedings in New York.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples of misconduct that have supported state discipline (and thus may predicate reciprocal USPTO discipline) include criminal convictions tied to professional misconduct, failure to notify other jurisdictions of suspensions, repeated registration/renewal delinquencies, and not participating in disciplinary proceedings. These factual findings are relevant to the Office when considering reciprocal measures.
